bottom_line: In men with chronic congestive heart failure receiving digoxin and a diuretic, hydralazine–isosorbide dinitrate vs placebo reduced cumulative mortality by two years (25.6 percent vs 34.3 percent) with an estimated 34 percent reduction in mortality risk (P<0.028).
implications: These data support that, in this trial population, hydralazine–isosorbide dinitrate was associated with lower cumulative mortality than placebo through two years (25.6 percent vs 34.3 percent) and an estimated 34 percent reduction in mortality risk (P<0.028; 95 percent confidence interval, 4 to 54 percent), while prazosin showed no mortality difference vs placebo. The study did not provide sufficient data to compare mortality beyond three years.

major_points.text: Double-blind randomized trial in men with chronic congestive heart failure on digoxin and a diuretic, comparing placebo, prazosin, or hydralazine plus isosorbide dinitrate.
major_points.quote: we randomly assigned 642 men with impaired car- diac function and reduced exercise tolerance who were taking digoxin and a diuretic to receive additional double- blind treatment with placebo, prazosin (20 mg per day), or the combination of hydralazine

major_points.text: Follow-up averaged 2.3 years (range 6 months to 5.7 years).
major_points.quote: Follow-up averaged 2.3 years (range, 6 months to 5.7 years).

major_points.text: The report emphasizes mortality as the primary end point and uses an intention-to-treat primary analysis.
major_points.quote: This report emphasizes the analysis of mortality, the primary end point.

major_points.text: At two years (a major end point specified in the protocol), hydralazine–nitrate showed an estimated 34% reduction in mortality risk vs placebo (P<0.028; 95% CI 4 to 54%).
major_points.quote: For the first two- year period, the Cox life-table regression model yield- ed an estimate of a cumulative reduction in mortality risk of 34 percent in the hydralazine-nitrate group, as compared with the placebo group (P<0.028; 95 per- cent confidence interval, 4 to 54 percent).

major_points.text: Prazosin mortality was similar to placebo.
major_points.quote: The mortality in the prazosin group was similar to that in the placebo group.

absolute_effects.text: Deaths during follow-up: placebo 120/273 (44.0 percent) vs hydralazine–nitrate 72/186 (38.7 percent).
absolute_effects.quote:
During the follow-up period, there were 120 deaths in the placebo group (44.0 percent), 91 deaths in
the prazosin group (49.7 percent), and 72 deaths in
the hydralazine—nitrate group (38.7 percent).

absolute_effects.text: Cumulative mortality at 2 years: placebo 34.3% vs hydralazine–isosorbide dinitrate 25.6%.
Cumulative mortality at 1 year: placebo 19.5% vs hydralazine–isosorbide dinitrate 12.1%.
Cumulative mortality at 3 years: placebo 46.9% vs hydralazine–isosorbide dinitrate 36.2%.

subgroups.text: Mortality was higher with coronary artery disease than without (P<0.02).
subgroups.quote: Mortality in the group with coronary artery disease was higher than that in the group without that dis- order (P<0.02; Fig. 2).

subgroups.text: No evidence that treatment had a differential influence on mortality by coronary artery disease status (interaction P = 0.47).
subgroups.quote: the hy- pothesis that therapy had a differential influence on mortality in these two subsets of patients was not sup- ported (P = 0.47 for a treatment-interaction term in the Cox regression model).

harms.text: Permanent discontinuation occurred in 47 patients (17%) in the placebo group (excluding discontinuations within one month before death).
harms.quote: Excluding the discontinuations that took place within one month before death, one or both types of placebo were dis- continued in 47 patients (17 percent) in the group receiving placebo
Prazosin was discontin- ued in 43 patients (23 percent).

harms.text: In the hydralazine–isosorbide dinitrate group, 31 patients (17%) stopped taking both drugs; additional patients discontinued hydralazine only or isosorbide dinitrate only.
harms.quote: In the hydralazine- isosorbide dinitrate group, 31 patients (17 percent) stopped taking both drugs, whereas 10 additional pa- tients discontinued hydralazine only and 19 discontin- ued isosorbide dinitrate only.

harms.text: Investigators classified 45% of the deaths as “sudden.”
harms.quote:
The in- vestigators classified 45 percent of the deaths as
“sudden.”

inclusion_criteria.quote: Recruitment was limited to men between the ages of 18 and 75.

inclusion_criteria.text: Evidence of cardiac dilatation defined by cardiothoracic ratio >0.55 or LV internal diameter in diastole >2.7 cm per square meter on echocardiography, or LV functional impairment with radionuclide ejection fraction <45 percent.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Eligibility for the trial was based on evidence of cardiac dilatation (cardiothoracic ratio >0.55 on chest x-ray film or a left ventricular internal diameter in diastole >2.7 cm per square meter on echocardiography) or left ventricular functional impairment (radionuclide ejection fraction <45 percent)

inclusion_criteria.text: Clinical and exercise stability on two consecutive visits separated by two weeks before randomization.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Clinical evaluations and exercise-tolerance tests on two consecutive visits (separated by two weeks) had to reveal clinical and exercise stability before randomization could take place.

exclusion_criteria.text: Exercise tolerance limited by chest pain rather than breathlessness and fatigue.
exclusion_criteria.quote: Patients were excluded from the study if exercise tolerance was limited by chest pain rather than by breathlessness and fatigue.

exclusion_criteria.text: Myocardial infarction within the previous three months.
exclusion_criteria.quote: Patients were also excluded if they had had a myocardial infarction within the previous three months

exclusion_criteria.text: Substantial obstructive valvular disease or considerable obstructive myocardial disease, chronic pulmonary disease, or other disease likely to limit five-year survival.
exclusion_criteria.quote: or if they had substantial obstruc- tive valvular disease or considerable obstructive myocardial disease, chronic pulmonary disease, or other disease likely to limit five-year survival.

exclusion_criteria.text: Required calcium antagonists, beta-blockers, or antihypertensive drugs other than diuretics.
exclusion_criteria.quote: or required calcium antagonists, beta-blockers, or antihyper- tensive drugs other than diuretics were excluded

exclusion_criteria.text: Administration of the study drugs was contraindicated.
exclusion_criteria.quote: as were patients in whom administration of the study drugs was contraindicated.

analysis_methods.text: Primary analysis included all study patients and all deaths according to intention-to-treat.
analysis_methods.quote: The primary analysis included all study patients and all deaths in their randomized treatment group, ac- cording to the intention-to-treat principle.

analysis_methods.text: Cumulative mortality curves calculated with life-table approach using the actuarial method.
analysis_methods.quote: The cumulative mortal- ity curves were calculated with the life-table approach by means of the actuarial method.

analysis_methods.text: Cox life-table regression model used for survival comparisons with adjustment for baseline variables.
analysis_methods.quote: To compare the treatment groups with re- spect to survival, the Cox life-table regression model was used when adjustments were made for-base-line variables.

analysis_methods.text: For unadjusted comparisons, log-rank and generalized Wilcoxon tests were used.
analysis_methods.quote: For unadjusted comparisons, two standard tests, the log-rank test and the general- ized Wilcoxon test, were used

analysis_methods.text: Sample size goal of 720 chosen to provide 84% power if either treatment reduced annual mortality to 33% below placebo.
analysis_methods.quote: The initial goal of a sample size of 720 patients was chosen to provide a power of 84 percent if either treatment reduced the annu- al mortality rate to 33 percent below that in the placebo group.

analysis_methods.text: O’Brien and Fleming multiple testing procedure used with four assessments for possible early stopping.
analysis_methods.quote: The method of O’Brien and Flem- ing, with four assessments for possible early stopping, was used to monitor the trial.

trial_conduct.quote: The study investigators had no knowledge of the results of the interim analyses of safety and efficacy; these aspects of the trial were moni- tored by the operations committee.

trial_conduct.text: Follow-up ended without early stopping on December 15, 1985.
trial_conduct.quote: Follow-up ended (without early stop- ping) on December 15, 1985.

criticisms.text: Because both hydralazine and isosorbide dinitrate were used in combination, the relative roles of the two agents cannot be defined.
criticisms.quote: Since both hydralazine, an arteriolar dilator,”° and isosorbide dinitrate, predominantly a venous dila- tor,?” were used in combination in the present trial, it is not possible to define the relative roles of the two agents.
